limitations_and_boundaries: The study cannot exclude the contribution of matrix stiffness combining with other paracrine cytokines to invadopodia formation.
The detailed interplay between integrin β1-based and Piezo1-based mechanosensory in invadopodia formation merits further investigation.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

experiments_or_tasks: In vivo subcutaneous animal model with filter membrane
Real-time migration analysis of HCC cells on 6, 10, 16 kPa substrates

methods.name: FN-coated polyacrylamide gels
methods.protocol_description: FN-coated polyacrylamide gels with stiffness of 6 kPa (low), 10 kPa (medium), and 16 kPa (high) were established for cell culture as previously described [28].

methods.name: Cell migration analysis using Cell IQ
methods.protocol_description: Migration trajectories of HCC cells were recorded and analyzed in real time using a Cell IQ living cell workstation for 48 h. 40 cells per group were randomly selected for statistical analysis.

methods.name: F-actin polymerization analysis
methods.protocol_description: HCC cells were stained with Alexa Fluo 488 phalloidin and DAPI, and F-actin polymerization was observed by confocal microscopy.

methods.name: In vitro matrix-gel invasion assay
methods.protocol_description: Matrigel, collagen I, and DMEM/MEM were mixed (25:11:14) to form a matrix-gel substrate. HCC cells were seeded on the surface and cultured for 4 days. Invasion depth was measured.

methods.name: In vivo subcutaneous invasion model
methods.protocol_description: HCC cells embedded in Matrigel/collagen I were wrapped in a polycarbonate filter membrane (8 μm pores) and transplanted subcutaneously into nude mice. After 10 days, tumors and membranes were collected for analysis.

study_units.name: Effect of matrix stiffness on migration and invasion

provenance.text_excerpt: The results demonstrated that increased matrix stiffness significantly improved the migration range and speed of HCC cells

results.value_raw_text: Increased matrix stiffness significantly improved the migration range and speed of HCC cells.

results.metric_name: Number of cells on filter membrane

provenance.text_excerpt: the number of the cells on filter membrane in shITGB1 and shPIEZO1 groups were all significantly decreased

results.value_raw_text: The number of cells on filter membrane in shITGB1 and shPIEZO1 groups were all significantly decreased.

provenance.text_excerpt: Compared with that of non-cell group, the surface of the matrix-gel substrate of HCC-WT group and HCC-shCtrl group all displayed obviously deep invaded-depth... however, the surface of the matrix-gel substrate of HCC-shITGB1 group and HCC-shPiezo1group exhibited relatively shallow invaded-depth, moreover Yoda1 intervention reversed the invasion phenotype

results.value_raw_text: HCC cells grown on matrix-gel substrate displayed obviously deep invaded-depth; shITGB1 and shPiezo1 groups exhibited relatively shallow invaded-depth, and Yoda1 intervention reversed this effect.

methods.name: Pharmacological interventions
methods.protocol_description: Gefitinib (EGFR inhibitor, 2 μmol/L), PP2 (Src inhibitor, 20 μmol/L), SB273005 (integrin αV/β5 inhibitor, 0.1 μmol/L), Yoda1 (Piezo1 agonist), GsMTx4 (Piezo1 antagonist) were applied as described.

methods.name: Western blot
methods.protocol_description: Total proteins extracted using RIPA buffer, separated by SDS-PAGE, transferred to PVDF membranes, probed with primary antibodies and HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies, and detected by ECL.

results.value_raw_text: Gefitinib decreased phosphorylation of EGFR, Src, cortactin and expression of Arg, MMP14 but not FAK; PP2 decreased phosphorylation of Src, cortactin and expression of Arg, MMP14 but not EGFR or FAK.

methods.name: Double immunofluorescent staining
methods.protocol_description: HCC cells were fixed, permeabilized, blocked, and incubated with cortactin antibody, then with Alexa Fluo 488 phalloidin and Alexa Fluor 594 secondary antibody. Punctate structures (yellow) at colocalization of cortactin and F-actin represent invadopodia.

methods.name: qRT-PCR
methods.protocol_description: Total RNA was extracted using Trizol, reverse transcribed, and amplified with specific primers. Relative expression normalized to GAPDH.

methods.name: Subcutaneous tumor model
methods.protocol_description: HCC cells (WT, shCtrl, shITGB1, shPiezo1) suspended in Matrigel/collagen I were injected subcutaneously into nude mice. Tumors were collected and analyzed for gene expression.

study_units.name: Matrix stiffness promotes invadopodia formation

provenance.text_excerpt: the number of invadopodia (yellow punctate structure) in HCC cell grown on high-stiffness substrate was significantly higher than that in HCC cells grown on low-stiffness substrate, and EGF intervention further increased the number of invadopodia

results.value_raw_text: The number of invadopodia in HCC cells grown on high-stiffness substrate was significantly higher than that on low-stiffness substrate; EGF intervention further increased the number.

provenance.text_excerpt: increased matrix stiffness evidently upregulated the expressions of invadopodia-associated proteins/genes (cortactin and MMP14), as well as the phosphorylation level of cortactin (Tyr421 and Tyr466), but little effect on EGF expression

results.value_raw_text: Increased matrix stiffness upregulated cortactin and MMP14 expression and cortactin phosphorylation (Tyr421, Tyr466), but little effect on EGF expression at cell level.

provenance.text_excerpt: the weight and volume of subcutaneous tumors in HCC-shITGB1 and HCC-shPiezo1 groups were all decreased compared with that in HCC-WT and HCC-shCtrl groups

results.value_raw_text: Weight and volume of subcutaneous tumors in shITGB1 and shPiezo1 groups were decreased compared with WT and shCtrl groups.
